Tuesday’s developments came amid tensions between Fazl and the federal government, which have been ongoing since mid-October.

Fazl had criticised the Centre for imposing governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and making the then-PTI provincial government non-functional. The JUI-F chief also accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the PML-N and PTI governments.

Tensions escalated when Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights, resulting in the veteran politician and key federal ministers exchanging harsh remarks against each other.

In recent weeks, PPP Chairman Bilawal-Bhutto Zardari — a key ally of the ruling PML-N — has voiced his support for Fazl and condemned the “government’s actions” against him.

Last week, police and Federal Constabulary (FC) personnel deployed to protect Fazl and other members of his family were withdrawn from the residences they guarded in Islamabad and Dera Ismail Khan.

JUI-F spokesman Aslam Ghouri had confirmed the withdrawal, alleging that the Maulana’s Islamabad residence had been cordoned off by capital police and that security personnel had harassed visitors. He also claimed that the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad had been besieged by police.

An Islamabad police official, however, said only one police guard had been withdrawn.

The JUI-F chief’s son has also come under scrutiny from the anti-graft watchdog, with the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) summoning former federal communications minister Asad Mahmood over alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 tenure. Mahmood skipped two consecutive summonses issued for Nov 10 and 14, according to a NAB source.

The JUI-F staged protests in parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Nov 7 against a “coordinated character assassination campaign” targeting Fazl.

Party leaders and workers condemned the alleged drone surveillance of his residence and the circulation of footage on social media, demanding an impartial investigation and action against those responsible.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz assures KP governor of continued support to eliminate terrorism
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday assured KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi of all possible cooperation on behalf of the federal government for the complete eradication of terrorism, durable peace and the welfare of the public in the province.

The premier made these remarks as he met with Kundi in Islamabad on Tuesday, according to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

During the meeting, he said that the sacrifices of the security forces and KP police in the war against terrorism in the province would not go in vain.

The federal government would continue to “fully support the implementation of the decisions taken at the apex committee meeting to completely eliminate terrorism”, he was quoted as saying.

He reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to providing full support for the development of KP and the welfare of its people, saying that all possible resources would be mobilised to provide them with healthcare, education and other basic facilities, according to the PMO.

The premier directed that special attention be given to improving social development indicators in KP, including healthcare and education.

He said that attention would also be given to promoting sports facilities in the province and providing young people with opportunities for constructive activities, the PMO added.

Meanwhile, Governor Kundi briefed the prime minister on the ongoing efforts by himself and the KP Advisory Council to improve law and order in the province.

Separately, Kundi also met with President Asif Ali Zardari, a statement by the President’s Office said, where he briefed the president on the situation following Oct 11, particularly the security situation.

The meetings come weeks after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament amid protests by the opposition.

On Oct 22, PM Shehbaz also chaired a meeting of the federal apex committee in Peshawar. He had vowed to take tough decisions, while reaffirming the Centre’s commitment to bringing peace to terrorism-hit districts in the province.

Last week, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir also reaffirmed the security forces “unwavering resolve” to decisively eliminate terrorism and preserve peace and stability of KP in close coordination with law enforcement agencies.

articles.title: Govt selects consortium of 3 foreign banks for $500m finance facility backed by MIGA
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The government on Tuesday selected a consortium of three foreign banks to arrange a $500 million trade finance facility, backed by the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), a member of the World Bank Group.

“Following a competitive selection process and receipt of bids from nine international financial institutions, the Finance Division, Government of Pakistan, has selected the following banks as financing partners for the facility,” the Ministry of Finance said in a statement.

The banks included Commerzbank, JP Morgan and Standard Chartered Bank. It added that this facility opened new avenues for international financing.

According to the ministry, the decision was taken in a virtual meeting held by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb with the senior leadership of a consortium of international banks and representatives of the agency.

The banks were selected on the basis of the most competitive financing terms offered to the government, it said.

“The one-year facility, renewable on a rolling 1+1+1 basis, will support the financing of essential imports and trade-related expenditures,” the statement said.

It noted that the transaction marked the government’s first-ever credit enhancement transaction with MIGA under its Trade Finance programme, while also representing the first-ever participation of Commerzbank and JP Morgan in commercial lending to the government.

“The strong response and participation from international financial institutions reflect growing confidence in Pakistan’s improving economic outlook and progress towards sustainable growth,” the ministry said, expressing the government’s appreciation for the interest shown by all participating institutions and its gratitude “for their time, effort and engagement throughout the process”.

It said the transaction marked an important step towards “mobilising private international capital through multilateral risk-mitigation instruments, diversifying external financing sources and exploring innovative financing structures, while maintaining prudent debt management and fiscal responsibility”.

The ministry said the government would work closely with MIGA and the selected banks to advance the transaction towards its timely execution, looking forward to building strong and lasting relationships.

articles.title: Reacting to Bilawal's remarks on 'brute majority', a section of legal community wants 26th, 27th Amendments repealed
articles.summary:
A hundred members of the legal fraternity and civil society have called for the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments to be repealed, reacting to remarks by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, whose party had made their enactment possible.

The 26th and 27th Amendments, enacted in October 2024 and November 2025 respectively, were passed by both houses of the Parliament amid outcry from the PTI-led opposition.

Last week, Bilawal — a strong advocate for both Amendments when they were passed — said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor mutual agreement; it was passed with brute majority”, and that the previous one did have mutual agreement.

He also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, noting that resignations of senior judges followed the legislation.

Later, the PPP chairman clarified that he was “not disowning” the 27th Amendment, but rather noting that it did not enjoy the same “unanimous consensus” as the 18th Amendment and the 1973 Constitution.

In an open letter on Tuesday, 100 individuals — mostly lawyers and also including activists and academics — called for both the 26th and 27th Amendments to be repealed.

“Pakistan’s constitutional order belongs to its people. It cannot be seized by a majority that its own members admit was never theirs to wield,” read the letter, also signed by retired Supreme Court Justice Mansoor Ali Shah.

The letter recalled that Bilawal “admitted that the 27th Amendment was passed neither through political consensus nor through agreement, but a ‘brute majority’”.

It demanded that the “constitutional order that existed prior to the 26th Amendment must be restored”, adding that any future reform of the judiciary must come through an “open and consultative process”.

The 26th Amendment carved a constitutional bench out of the SC, with its members chosen by a reconstituted Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) in which judges no longer held a majority.

A year later, the 27th Amendment turned those benches into an entirely separate court, the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), which is said to have effectively dethroned the SC as the country’s highest judicial forum.

It also made significant changes to the judicial system and the military’s chain of command, and granted immunities to government officials. Two of the SC’s senior-most judges, including Shah, resigned in protest the day it became law.

Tuesday’s letter also called for reserved seats in the legislative houses to be returned to their “lawful claimants”, in an apparent reference to the opposition.

The PTI was deprived of its reserved seats in the 2024 elections following the revocation of its electoral symbol.

Although an SC bench declared the PTI eligible for the seats, the order was not implemented and later overturned by the constitutional bench created via the 26th Amendment, which handed them to the coalition parties that challenged the 2024 ruling.

“The government cannot continue exercising parliamentary authority derived from a process that the governing coalition’s own leadership has now publicly called into question,” Tuesday’s letter read.

“These seats must be restored to their rightful claimants through the appropriate legal and constitutional mechanism,” it added.

The letter noted that Bilawal “described the way the opposition was stripped of its reserved seats as ‘a joke’ and said the treasury benches had simply put those seats ‘in their pockets’”.

“Most damning of all, he accused the ruling government of amending the Constitution using seats that are ‘not yours’,” the document added.

The signatories pointed out that these words came “from the government’s key coalition partner whose votes were required to pass both the 26th and 27th Amendments”.

It continued: “The treasury benches face a question they can no longer evade. Their own coalition partner says reserved seats were taken by parties that had no right to them.

“On what constitutional, legal or moral basis does the government then keep claiming the numbers through which the 26th and 27th Amendments were passed?”

The lawyers and activists noted that a two-thirds majority was the safeguard the Constitution demands so that “it cannot be changed without the genuine and lawful representation of the people’s will”.

However, a majority “made up with seats that were unjustly denied to the opposition is not the majority the Constitution demands”, they contended.

“An amendment passed on that basis holds no constitutional, legal, or democratic validity. An amendment passed without a legitimate two-thirds majority is void from its very inception,” the letter asserted.

It further said that these questions applied directly to the FCC, which “owes its existence wholly to the 27th Amendment”.

“Its jurisdiction, its composition and its authority all come from a constitutional change whose legitimacy is now openly repudiated by the very people who brought it into being.

“A court cannot rise higher than its source. An institution whose authors cannot defend how it was built has no foundation left to stand on,” the lawyer said.

“Pakistan has witnessed far too many admissions of wrongdoing that have led to no consequences,” the letter observed, noting that leaders acknowledge violations at press conferences, express reservations, and then “allow the very arrangements they condemn to continue unchanged”.

“This cycle must end. The question is no longer simply whether a wrong was committed, but whether consequences and meaningful action will follow.”

The signatories stressed this was a “moment to begin repairing the grave damage caused to the judiciary and the constitutional order”.

“Those in power have a choice. They can either continue to cling to an illegitimate majority or they can correct course.”

The signatories include former Sindh High Court Bar Association president Salahuddin Ahmed, ex-minister Shireen Mazari, ex-senator Afrasiab Khattak, ex-MNA Bushra Gohar, HRCP Chairperson Nasir Zaidi and economist Dr Kaiser Bengali.

The lawyers include Rida Hosain, Hassan Abdullah Niazi, Asad Rahim Khan, Abdul Moiz Jaferii, Khadija Siddiqi, Faisal Siddiqi, Abuzar Salman Khan Niazi and Zainab Shahid.

Rights activists, including Nighat Dad and Usama Khilji, and members of the Women’s Action Forum (WAF) were among other signatories.

articles.title: Punjab Assembly adopts resolution seeking tougher punishment for blasphemy
articles.summary:
LAHORE: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday unanimously passed a resolution demanding legislation to make the punishment harsher under Section 298-A (use of derogatory remarks, etc, in respect of holy personages) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

Currently, Section 298-A provides “imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years”, or fine, or both as punishment for “whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by visible representation, or by any imputation, innuendo or insinuation, directly or indirectly, defiles the sacred name of any wife (Ummul Mumineen) or members of the family (Ahl-i-bait) of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him), or any of the righteous Caliphs (Khulafa-i-Rashideen) or companions (Sahaaba) of the Holy Prophet”.

The resolution, moved in the House by opposition MPA Rana Aurangzaib, contended that the existing penalty was “insufficient” for such an act which “hurts religious sentiments”.

The House urged the federal government to move on the matter on a “priority basis” and enact legislation needed to increase the penalty under Section 298-A.

It also called on the federal government to ensure effective lawmaking and implementation to uphold respect for religious sanctities and to maintain social peace and harmony.

In August 2023, Parliament passed the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill 2023 to increase the punishment under Section 298-A from three years of imprisonment to at least 10 years in jail.

However, then-president Arif Alvi returned the bill to Parliament.

The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan had noted that the bill would have made it “more difficult for the accused to obtain statutory bail, which will now be granted at the discretion of the court rather than as a legal right”.

It observed that “in general, blasphemy cases are often lodged by the police under pressure from far-right clerics or complainants with personal vendettas or to stem the risk of mob violence following mere allegations of blasphemy”.

articles.title: Balochistan govt announces rewards of up to Rs250m for information on wanted terrorists
articles.summary:
QUETTA: The Balochistan government has announced rewards ranging from Rs500,000 to Rs250 million for providing authentic information about most-wanted terrorists in the province.

According to an official advertisement issued by the provincial government, a reward of Rs250m has been fixed for information about Bashir Zeb of the banned Balochistan Liberation Army and Abdul Rehman alias Rehman Gul.

Similar rewards have been fixed for other wanted persons depending on their status.

List of most-wanted terrorists and respective rewards on information regarding them issued by the provincial government. — via Saleem Shahid

The government said the list has been issued as part of its efforts to maintain law and order and eliminate terrorism in the province.

Balochistan Home Affairs Adviser Babar Yousafzai affirmed that the provincial government was determined to eradicate terrorism and protect the lives and properties of citizens.

The list of most-wanted terrorists and the announcement of rewards were, therefore, part of the ongoing government measures against terrorism.

Yousafzai stressed that public cooperation was of utmost importance in the war against terrorism.

The adviser appealed to the public to contact the relevant institutions of the government if they had any authentic information regarding the wanted terrorists.

He said the identity of informants would be kept anonymous, and immediate action would be taken against the terrorists. Payment of rewards would be made according to the rules and regulations fixed by the government.

Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, since the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks.

While Pakistan recorded fewer militant attacks from Nov 6 to 12, fatalities and injuries increased sharply, “highlighting the changing intensity and continued volatility of militant threat across the country”, according to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies.

Balochistan recorded 13 attacks, resulting in eight deaths and 19 injuries, while KP “remained the principal centre of violence” with 16 attacks and 44 fatalities.

articles.title: Hours-long road closures around Karachi’s PIDC junction cause traffic congestion
articles.summary:
KARACHI: Commuters in Karachi’s Saddar area faced traffic congestion on Tuesday after authorities closed some roads around the PIDC junction for a few hours in response to a sit-in call by the Sindh Indus Lawyers Forum (SILF).

In an alert issued at 1:16pm, Karachi Traffic Police said both roads from PIDC Chowk towards the State Life Building, as well as Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road, were closed to traffic.

In an update at around 6pm, the traffic police said the cut from PIDC Chowk towards State Life Building and both sides of Dr Ziauddin Ahmed Road have been reopened to commuters.

As an alternative route, traffic was previously being diverted from PIDC Chowk towards Club Road and from the State Life Building towards Beaumont Road.

This screengrab from Google Maps shows traffic near the PIDC junction at around 4:30pm on Nov 24, 2026.

According to a statement issued by SILF, lawyers staged a sit-in outside the Sindh High Court.

They also staged a rally from Shahrah-i-Liaquat towards CM House through Court Road, Sindh Secretariat Chowk, Sindh Assembly and Aiwan-i-Sadr Road.

The forum has put forward 16 demands under the banner of ‘Sindh Demands’, including opposition to the division of Sindh and the construction of Jalalpur Canal.

The protest call comes as a debate over a “system reset” in the country has intensified over the past few months. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units, arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

The PML-N-led federal government has insisted on holding a referendum across the country on the establishment of new provinces or administrative units.

However, the suggestion has faced severe backlash from its ally PPP, with party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari saying that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

SILF said its demands also include “opposition to constitutional amendments and the proposed amendment”, apparently referring to the 26th and 27th Amendments, though no new amendment has been officially proposed.

Moreover, SILF’s demands, according to its statement, include stopping alleged irregularities in the Sindh Public Service Commission and alleged government intervention in lawyers’ bars.

“Corporate farming and mining in Karoonjhar mountain should be stopped and political prisoners should be released,” SILF further said.

On Sunday, a large number of people from across Sindh took to the streets of Karachi in a rally organised by the Jeay Sindh Rahbar Committee, an alliance of four nationalist parties, to protest against any plan for the creation of new provinces or administrative units in Sindh.

articles.title: Sales tax zones being established in Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan, PM told
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was informed on Tuesday that separate sales tax zones were being established in the country’s four major taxpayer units — Karachi, Lahore, Islamabad and Multan — to improve collection.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the development was shared during a weekly review meeting concerning the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) in Islamabad.

The move comes as the government has decided to reverse the functional integration of sales tax and income tax collection after 17 years, acknowledging that the sales tax revenue gap has widened to Rs3.4 trillion amid weak enforcement and poor revenue collection.

The statement released on Tuesday said that the meeting was also informed that work was underway to establish a modern cargo tracking system to address the sales tax gap and curb smuggling.

The system would digitally track the movement of goods from loading to delivery and comprise an electronic consignment note, a risk management system, field enforcement and an analytics dashboard, the statement said.

A steering committee with provincial representation was also being formed to oversee the system’s implementation, the PMO said.

The meeting was further informed that the FBR was establishing an office at Karachi’s Korangi Industrial Estate to provide services to local industrialists at their doorstep.

According to the PMO, PM Shehbaz directed authorities to expedite customs clearance, immigration and other operations at the country’s airports and make smart scanning systems operational at all international airports.

The meeting was informed that smart scanning systems were being installed at major international airports with the support of relevant agencies. The systems would automatically direct passengers’ baggage to the green or red channels.

The prime minister expressed the hope that the FBR chairman’s recent visits to Karachi and Lahore and meetings with local traders and industrialists would yield positive results for trade, exports and investment.

The meeting was informed that an audit of oil marketing companies’ bonded warehouses, conducted on the prime minister’s directives, had uncovered irregularities amounting to Rs24.4 billion. Recoveries were being made through legal procedures, the statement said.

It added that PM Shehbaz directed authorities to take action and make recoveries without discrimination.

The meeting was further informed that the Indus Collectorate had begun operations at bridges over the Indus River across the country. The enforcement collectorate, which had 856 staff members, had seized illegal goods worth Rs1.849bn in 302 operations so far, the statement said.

Regarding Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited (PRAL), the meeting was informed that additional security features had been incorporated into several software systems to ensure data integrity. Departmental action was also being taken against FBR officers who had previously issued unauthorised consumption certificates under the FATA/PATA tax exemption, the statement said.

In 2009, the government transferred the administration of sales tax and federal excise duty from Customs to the Inland Revenue Service (IRS) as part of a World Bank-backed reform aimed at integrating tax administration.

However, after 17 years of integration, the sales tax revenue gap has widened to an estimated Rs3.4tr, compared with Rs2tr for income tax, raising questions about the effectiveness of the arrangement.

Under the new arrangement, specialised officers will handle sales tax and income tax separately, while both will continue to be administered within the IRS rather than through separate services.

articles.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill 7, including senior security official
articles.summary:
Israeli airstrikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed seven people, including Hamas’s director of internal security, Palestinian officials in the territory told AFP, despite a ceasefire in place since last year.

Israel’s military said it had struck a senior Hamas official.

Gaza’s interior ministry said an airstrike in Gaza City killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahal, director-general of the Internal Security Service.

Mahmoud Bassal, spokesman for Gaza’s civil defence agency, told AFP that several other people were in critical condition following the same strike in Gaza City’s Rimal neighbourhood.

The strike comes as talks are underway in Israel to form a new government after October legislative elections produced no clear winner.

Centrist Gadi Eisenkot wants to form a coalition to end caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s long tenure.

But Netanyahu, who has staked his reputation on ensuring security for Israel after the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023, remains in charge of military operations while negotiations continue.

Police station strike

Bassal said earlier on Tuesday that three people, including a 17-year-old, had been killed in a separate Israeli airstrike near Gaza City.

Three more were also killed in a third airstrike on a police station in the Al-Mawasi area in southern Gaza, he added.

Gaza’s police force said two policemen aged 23 and 33 were among the dead.

It condemned the strike as “part of an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus”.

Israel’s military said it “struck terrorists in the area” of the police station, but did not confirm the strike that killed the 17-year-old.

Israel and Hamas regularly accuse each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by the October 2023 attack.

More than 1,650 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the truce, according to an AFP tally based on data from the Gaza health ministry.

In the same period, the Israeli military says seven of its soldiers have been killed, as well as one civilian contractor. Most of Gaza’s population of 2.1 million live displaced in tents or makeshift shelters in the territory, where Israel’s military says it controls more than 60 per cent of the land.

articles.title: Freedom of speech should not become a shield for those crossing 'red lines', says Naqvi
articles.summary:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Tuesday asserted that freedom of speech should not become a shield for those who cross “red lines”.

He made the remarks while addressing a seminar organised by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI).

At the outset of his speech, the minister said that there were four “red lines” for the state: terrorism, hate speech, incitement to violence and sexual exploitation of children.

“On these four points, there is no compromise. Pakistan has paid for terrorism in blood. As interior minister, I have attended the funerals of martyrs. And very often, the hate that killed them began on a mobile phone,” he said.

He alleged that only 47 per cent of the complaints made by the Counter Terrorism Department were acted upon by social media platforms.

“This is not about technology, this is about people. We are not saying that free speech must be curtailed […] journalists must report, citizens must question, dissent must be heard, including against the government, but freedom of speech can never become a shield for those who cross these red lines,” he said.

He went on to say that Pakistan had “limited manpower”, resources and technology. Giving the example of Punjab, he said that the province had a population of 140 million against a strength of 61 people in the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA).

“And these 61 people include drivers, clerks and officers. We cannot do this alone. That is why we have established a Social Media Protection Regulatory Authority,” he said.

The minister called for moving from policy towards enforcement.

“To begin with [social media] platforms, OTT services and major content creators must register with the authority. Registration is not a licence to silence anyone, it tells us who is accountable when something goes wrong,” he said.

He said that every social media platform “must name an empowered representative for Pakistan, who can actually take decisions”.

“Similarly, citizens need one complaint channel they can track. We are moving all NCCIA complaints onto the Pak ID app and the authority is building a single fully tracked complaint system,” he said.

Naqvi then went on to recount a recent town hall meeting, where he met five girls who were on the verge of ending their lives due to someone about to release “sensitive material” on social media platforms.

“We don’t have any pathway for approaching those platforms. It’s their responsibility to react immediately to save these innocent lives,” he said.

The minister said that the social media authority would verify whether action had been taken or not.

“Finally, enforcement will be step by step: engagement, then notice, then penalties. Blocking a whole [social media] platform will remain a last resort … our request will be clear, lawful and open to review,” he said.

“The state should not feel helpless. Yet, we see terrorist groups still recruiting, still raising terrorist funds, still spreading fear on these very platforms,” he said.

Giving an example, Naqvi said that the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) was a declared terrorist organisation, yet “many of their officials are still using these platforms”.

“If it is a declared [terrorist] organisation, then who allows them to move around and use all these platforms? Someone needs to stop [them]. This is our request,” he said.

“If you are not doing it, what meaning should we take? If it is declared by your country that this organisation is a blacklisted organisation, is a terrorist organisation and then you don’t take action, there’s a big question mark,” he said. He added that the government was focusing on the capacity building of the NCCIA.

“Today, I extend an open hand to all these platforms. Let us sit together, not across the table. Operate globally, be accountable globally and never let Pakistani citizens feel unheard,” he concluded.

articles.title: Eight killed, seven injured as passenger vehicle plunges into ravine in KP's Torghar
articles.summary:
At least eight people, including two women, were killed and seven others injured on Tuesday when a passenger vehicle plunged into a deep ravine in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Torghar district, Rescue 1122 said.

The accident occurred at Kundo Gigianay in Shatal Sira as the vehicle was travelling towards Jadba, according to the rescue service.

Rescue 1122 said the vehicle’s brakes reportedly failed, causing it to plunge into the ravine.

The injured included three men, three women and a child.

Rescue personnel shifted them to a basic health unit (BHU), where they received initial medical treatment, before transferring them to the District Headquarters Hospital in Battagram by ambulance for further treatment.

Three ambulances and 10 rescue personnel took part in the operation, Rescue 1122 said.

Earlier this month, three people were killed and 13 others injured when a coach collided with a motorcycle in Dera Ismail Khan.

The coach was carrying members of a Tablighi Jamaat group.

Earlier in the month, at least eight people were also killed and 30 others injured when a passenger bus collided with a truck near the Havelian Interchange on Hazara Motorway.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz congratulates CDF Munir on Hall of Fame induction at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday congratulated Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on his induction into the Hall of Fame at Malaysia’s National Defence Studies Centre.

“This distinction also reflects the enduring friendship between Pakistan and Malaysia,” the premier said on X.

“Field Marshal’s resolute leadership during Marka-i-Haq, unwavering commitment to national defence, invaluable contributions to promoting peace, and enhancing Pakistan’s standing internationally makes this honour truly befitting,” he added.

CDF Munir is on an official visit to Malaysia. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the visit aims to further strengthen bilateral defence and military cooperation between the two countries.

On Monday, ISPR said CDF Munir would also visit the National Defence Studies Centre, where a formal ceremony would be held to induct him as the 21st member of its “prestigious” Hall of Fame.

According to PM Shehbaz, the recognition belongs equally to the “brave” men and women of Pakistan’s armed forces, “whose courage, dedication and sacrifices safeguard our beloved homeland, and to the people of Pakistan, whose resilience and unwavering support remain our greatest strength”.

In a meeting with Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim on Monday, CDF Munir reaffirmed their shared commitment to strengthening bilateral defence ties in Putrajaya. CDF Munir also held a meeting with Malaysian Defence Minister Mohamed Khaled bin Nordin.

Last week, Malaysian High Commissioner Datuk Mohammad Azhar Mazlan reaffirmed his country’s commitment to strengthening its strategic partnership with Pakistan, highlighting longstanding political, economic, defence and cultural ties between the two countries.

He was addressing a gathering of Pakistani media representatives and members of the Malaysian community at the Malaysian High Commission.

In August, Pakistan and Malaysia agreed to establish a joint working group between their interior ministries to promote institutional cooperation, with a focus on counter-terrorism, counter-narcotics, cybercrime and the prevention of illegal immigration.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz takes notice of provocative statements by cabinet members, urges them to settle differences amicably
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: Amid rising political tensions, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday took notice of provocative statements by the federal cabinet members against each other and directed them to resolve their differences through consultation.

The remarks come amid a war of words between coalition partners over the past few days regarding a proposed referendum on the creation of new provinces, with a federal cabinet member publicly expressing his grievances against a colleague.

On Monday, PML-N Senator Rana Sanaullah said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had “complicated” the matter of creating new provinces by making an “irrelevant speech at an irrelevant forum”.

In his remarks, Sanaullah, who also holds the portfolio of inter-provi­ncial coordination, stood by his earlier criticism of the interior minister’s choice to start the debate on provinces while addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit in Islamabad in July.

Naqvi had whipped up a political storm by calling for creating new administrative units in the country to “reset” the current “system” of governance. Following Sanaullah’s earlier remarks, Naqvi, without naming Sanaullah had warned last week, “The day I comment on this minister, he will not be able to show his face.”

In a statement issued by the PM Office on Tuesday, the prime minister took notice of recent statements by ministers and said the federal government’s entire focus was on public welfare projects.

“The government is continuing its journey from economic stability towards sustainable economic growth,” the prime minister said.

The prime minister said the federal government has always promoted the politics of development and progress.

“On this occasion, I direct all federal cabinet ministers to refrain from making political statements against one another,” the prime minister added.

“Matters among federal cabinet members should be resolved through mutual understanding and consensus,” the prime minister said.

He said statements by federal ministers against one another create a negative impression and divert attention from the politics of development and progress.

PM Shehbaz said federal cabinet ministers were performing well and should remain focused on public service, development and progress.

He said representatives of provincial governments should also refrain from making such statements and promote constructive dialogue.

“Statements against one another must cease completely. It is our collective responsibility to play an effective role in ensuring political stability,” the premier said.

Speaking to Geo News on Monday, Sanaullah had said it was his right as a colleague and as a political worker to express his opinion on Naqvi’s work.

The PM’s adviser contended that his colleague’s remarks at the business forum “complicated this issue, and today the matter… has become extremely controversial”.

“Now, if it comes to parliament, it will arrive in a controversial state,” he observed, affirming that his party will make all possible efforts to build a consensus.

The development came against the backdrop of a proposed referendum over the creation of new provinces. The issue gained renewed attention after PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari opposed the creation of new provinces and the proposed referendum in a speech on Tuesday, warning that any “forced” attempt to divide provinces, particularly Sindh, could lead to bloodshed.

The federal government, however, maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional means of gauging public opinion on the creation of new provinces. Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry also insisted last week that a referendum on the matter “will happen”.

On November 12, Naqvi had floated the idea of holding a referendum to gauge public opinion on the issue, saying the exercise could settle the contentious debate once and for all.

articles.title: Cricket's saliva ban to stay despite Indian skipper Shubman Gill’s call to overturn rule
articles.summary:
The International Cricket Council has no plans to reverse the ban on applying saliva to shine the ball, despite India skipper Shubman Gill’s call to allow the practice again.

Gill on Monday said the ban should be revoked to help bowlers get reverse swing, after India’s high-scoring opening Test in Wellington against New Zealand ended in a draw.

However, AFP understands that the ICC has no immediate plans to relax the rule, which is treated in the same way as any other unfair method of changing the ball’s condition.

Saliva can materially alter the ball when mixed with sweets, chewing gum and mints and the practice is incredibly hard to monitor and regulate.

The ICC temporarily barred the practice of applying saliva as a precautionary measure during the pandemic in 2020 and two years later made it permanent.

The use of saliva to shine one side of the old ball and keep the other rough helps fast bowlers get the leather ball to swing late.

“I don’t understand why we haven’t been allowed to shine the ball yet – we are way past Covid times,” Gill said after the draw. “There was a rule that you can’t put saliva on the ball to make it shine. It’s been seven-eight years and I still don’t understand why they are not allowing it.

“I think this is also a big factor (in bowlers struggling to get wickets).” 

The tourists had declared their first innings on a mammoth 720-9 midway through the fourth day, but New Zealand survived 120 overs to finish on 239-5 at the close.

The Indian Premier League lifted its saliva ban last year, much to the bowlers’ delight, but the ICC finds no reason to relax it in international matches.

India and New Zealand now head to Christchurch for the second and deciding Test starting Friday, where both captains expect a more typical green, grassy and seamer-friendly wicket

articles.title: Imran wants PTI to expand political alliance, extend outreach to Fazl and other opposition parties, core committee told
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The PTI’s core committee has been informed that incarcerated party founder Imran Khan wanted it to expand its “political alliance” and extend outreach to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties.

Imran’s instructions were conveyed to the committee during an overnight meeting that began on Monday and during which lawyer Latif Khosa briefed the members on his meeting with Imran and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, at the Adiala jail earlier this month.

Khosa, along with another of Imran’s lawyers, Salman Safdar, was allowed to meet Imran and Bushra Bibi on Nov 11. The meeting, which was said to have lasted three hours, included discussions on Imran’s health, cases against him and the possible 28th constitutional amendment, the lawyers had said.

The PTI issued a statement after Khosa briefed the party’s core committee on the meeting.

“The core committee was informed that Imran Khan had expressed his complete confidence in the opposition leadership. He directed that the political alliance be further expanded and that outreach be extended to Maulana Fazlur Rehman and other opposition parties, with the objective of forming a broader political alliance and initiating vigorous political activities,” the statement said.

Early in November, leaders of opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen-i-Pakistan, which includes the PTI, had met Fazl and the two sides had agreed to strengthen their alliance and parliamentary coordination.

Opposition parties appear to have increased coordination after the Oct 11 imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa — where the PTI had been in power — which also drew criticism from Fazl.

Meanwhile, tensions between the JUI-F chief and the federal government have escalated since mid-October, with Fazl accusing the Centre of reneging on its commitments despite his efforts to mediate between the ruling PML-N in the Centre and the PTI.

New provinces

Khosa also briefed the PTI core committee meeting, which was chaired by party chairperson Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, on Imran’s instruction regarding the debate on creating new provinces.

The committee was informed that Imran had instructed that the matter concerning the creation of new provinces be “deliberated upon in detail at the forthcoming meeting of PTI’s parliamentary party”.

The recommendations formulated following those deliberations would subsequently be presented to Imran for his decision, the statement said.

Imran’s health

The committee was also briefed on Imran’s health and “expressed serious concern over their medical condition” and demanded the immediate implementation of the Supreme Court’s decision of Aug 18, in which the authorities had been directed to transfer Imran to Shifa International Hospital, a private health facility in Islamabad.

The committee also demanded the immediate implementation of judicial orders concerning Bushra Bibi’s medical treatment.

Earlier this month, the Islamabad High Court had directed proper medical care and hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi, in line with prison rules.

The statement also referred to a recent letter written by Imran to top judges, saying that the core committee expressed “deep concern over the apprehensions raised by Imran Khan regarding his health and medical treatment”.

Reiterating its previous demands, the committee “urged the honourable judges to take immediate and serious notice of the matters raised in Imran Khan’s letter and ensure the prompt implementation of judicial orders concerning his medical treatment”, the statement said.

The committee also called on “the chief justice to […] ensure unrestricted access of Imran Khan’s personal physicians to him and facilitate his comprehensive medical examination and appropriate treatment”.

“Imran Khan must also be granted access to his family members and legal representatives. The committee emphasised that his health requires urgent judicial attention and that any further delay is unacceptable,” the statement said.

Detentions

Moreover, the committee “strongly condemned the continued detention” of Sohail Afridi — who has been rendered non-functional as the KP chief minister following the imposition of governor’s rule — and other PTI lawmakers.

“The committee particularly condemned the extension of detention orders under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) against elected representatives and political workers” and maintained that the “continued detention of elected representatives and political workers, and restrictions on their political activities, are contrary to fundamental constitutional, democratic and human rights”, the statement said.

The core committee appealed to the Federal Constitutional Court and its chief justice to “suitably modify the existing stay order concerning Section 3 of the MPO and provide relief to political leaders and workers who had been granted bail by the Peshawar High Court before Nov 5 but whose release orders remain unimplemented owing to the stay order”.

The committee demanded the immediate removal of legal impediments preventing their release, the statement said.

The committee also decided to observe Nov 26 as the “Martyrs’ Day” to commemorate the loss of lives during the 2024 protests.

In the protests in Islamabad on Nov 26, 2024, deaths were reported among both the protesters and the security personnel.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on December 16 on state carrier
articles.summary:
Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on December 16, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday, though the government said she can only return through extradition.

It is the first time Hasina, 79, has set a specific date for her return, potentially raising political and legal tensions in a country where her party is banned and where violence has risen since she sought a new passport and other documents earlier this month.

In addition to seeking the paperwork, cancelled months after she fled to Delhi following the uprising against her, Hasina has urged the Bangladeshi government to arrange her return on flag carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines.

“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, said in a statement.

“Having exiled her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on December 16th.” The government, however, reiterated that she can only be extradited by India, having been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising. Hasina has denied the charges from exile.

“She can only return home by extradition treaty; in handcuffs, and under strict surveillance,” Humaiun Kobir, Bangladesh’s minister of state for foreign affairs, told Reuters.

India’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April, the ministry said it was examining Bangladesh’s extradition request and wanted to “engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties”.

On the request to arrange a flight, Kobir said: “Bangladesh will not entertain any such delusional request”.

Aminul Islam, chief prosecutor of Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal, which sentenced Hasina to death, said it was unreasonable for a convicted fugitive to expect the government to arrange her return.

A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would be arrested and jailed on return and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back.

The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced her out of power.

articles.summary:
• Vows political office, influence won’t shield offenders    • INEC warns against turning campaigns into battlefield 

• NDC boycotts security meeting, seeks international intervention

 

From Molly Kilete and Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja

Alarmed by the escalating wave of political violence, killings, intimidation and attacks on opposition figures ahead of the 2027 general elections, the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, yesterday read the riot act to the political class, vowing to investigate and prosecute politicians who recruit, finance and deploy thugs to unleash violence on their opponents, irrespective of their political offices, affiliations or influence.

Disu, who declared that the Force would no longer fold its arms and allow politicians and their supporters to take the law into their own hands, warned that no political ambition was worth the life of any Nigerian and no electoral victory justified the destruction of national peace.

The warning came as Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, raised the alarm over persistent violations of electoral laws by political actors, warning that growing incidents of violence, intimidation and attacks on citizens and members of political parties threatened the credibility of the forthcoming elections.

However, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) boycotted the high-level security meeting convened by the IGP, accusing the police and other security agencies of complicity in attacks on its members allegedly perpetrated by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), and calling for international intervention to safeguard democratic participation in Nigeria.

Speaking at the security meeting held at the Force Headquarters, Abuja, which brought together national chairmen, secretaries and executives of registered political parties, representatives of security agencies, civil society organisations, INEC officials and other stakeholders, Disu expressed concern over the increasing incidents of violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues, intimidation of political opponents, use of dangerous weapons and disruption of lawful political gatherings.

He warned that such developments endangered innocent lives, threatened public peace and undermined confidence in democratic institutions.

Declaring zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the parties, candidates or individuals involved, the IGP assured political parties and their supporters of adequate protection to exercise their democratic rights, including organising rallies, holding meetings and expressing their political preferences without fear or intimidation.

“Our neutrality in the political process is non-negotiable. We owe allegiance to the Constitution, the law and the Nigerian people, not any political party or individual,” he said.

Disu warned that the recruitment, financing and deployment of political thugs, threats of violence, attacks on electoral officials and destruction of electoral materials would attract appropriate law enforcement action, insisting that political office, party affiliation and personal influence would not place anyone above the law.He assured Nigerians that offenders would be professionally investigated and prosecuted in accordance with due process, while every political party and candidate would be accorded equal treatment under the law.

Beyond the responsibilities of security agencies, the IGP charged political party leaders to take responsibility for the conduct of their candidates, youth wings and supporters, urging national chairmen to issue clear directives against violence and ensure compliance across their party structures.

He also called on national secretaries to facilitate effective communication and ensure compliance with applicable electoral notification requirements, while urging youth leaders to mobilise young people for constructive democratic participation rather than expose them to manipulation and political violence.

Disu stressed that peaceful political competition remained essential to democratic development, urging stakeholders to place the lives of Nigerians and the stability of the country above partisan interests.

•INEC raises alarm over electoral law violations

Amupitan, who described the growing incidents of political violence and violations of electoral laws as worrisome, warned politicians against turning electioneering into a battlefield, urging them to concentrate on presenting their manifestos, policies and ideas to Nigerians rather than resorting to violence and intimidation in their quest for power.

The INEC chairman said strict compliance with electoral laws and procedures had become imperative as political activities intensified ahead of the 2027 general elections, stressing that the credibility of the polls depended not only on the integrity of the voting process but also on the political environment in which campaigns and other electoral activities were conducted.

Recalling his earlier engagement with political party leaders and members of the National Peace Committee on August 18, 2026, where he emphasised the need for peaceful political competition, Amupitan warned that when political actors could no longer freely assemble, organise campaigns or express their views without fear of intimidation, the democratic process was already being undermined before election day.

He noted that persistent attacks on political party members and other citizens could discourage voter participation and weaken public confidence in the electoral process, urging political stakeholders to operate within the boundaries established by the Constitution and electoral laws.

Amupitan reminded politicians and their supporters that the people whose votes they sought were the ultimate holders of sovereign power under the Constitution and that all stakeholders had a responsibility to protect their rights, security and welfare.

•NDC accuses police of partisanship

Despite Disu’s assurances of neutrality and equal protection for political parties, the NDC said its decision to boycott the security meeting followed repeated attacks on its members across the country and the alleged failure of security agencies to apprehend and prosecute those responsible.

In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the party accused the police of abandoning their constitutional responsibility to protect all Nigerians, irrespective of their political affiliations.

“We no longer feel safe and protected by a Police Force that watches helplessly the slaughter of our members across the country by hired thugs of the ruling APC. We will not lend legitimacy to a process that has failed to protect us,” it said.

The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Cross River, Enugu and Delta states, alleging that its members had come under sustained attacks and that political campaigns were increasingly being characterised by violence and intimidation.

It particularly recalled the alleged prevention of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State by thugs loyal to the APC government and the reported killing of four of its members in Delta State.

“The killing of four members of the NDC in Delta State was done in the full glare of the Police and security forces who were supposed to protect all Nigerians,” the party alleged.

Accusing the police of partisan conduct, the NDC declared that the Nigeria Police Force had become an “APC Police sustained by taxpayers’ money”. It also faulted the police over what it described as their inability to conduct proper investigations into attacks on opposition politicians and ensure that perpetrators were brought to justice.

The party called on the international community to prevail on President Bola Tinubu and the APC-led government to uphold democratic standards, warning that democracy could not survive in an atmosphere where opposition members were attacked and killed with impunity.

“The NDC remains committed to peaceful, issue-based campaigns, but we will not be intimidated, silenced, or chased out of the democratic space,” it added.

The allegations have not been independently verified. Although Disu reaffirmed the neutrality of the police, his reported remarks at the security meeting did not specifically address the NDC’s wider accusations.

•Mounting concerns over political violence

The security meeting came against the backdrop of growing incidents of political violence across the country, with attacks on campaign rallies, political gatherings, candidates and their supporters heightening apprehension over the conduct of the forthcoming elections.

President Bola Tinubu had, on November 13, condemned the growing incidents of campaign violence and directed security agencies to deal firmly with perpetrators, irrespective of their political affiliations.

Similarly, the Senate, last week, called for investigations into attacks on political actors and urged INEC to enforce relevant provisions of the Electoral Act against perpetrators of political violence.

The upper legislative chamber also urged state governors to desist from denying opposition political parties access to public facilities for campaigns and other legitimate political activities.

The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) had also given INEC seven days to initiate the prosecution of suspected perpetrators of electoral violence against whom sufficient evidence existed or face legal action.

articles.title: Billboard controversy: Senator Kalu’s politics anchored in people, not billboards –Group
articles.summary:
Reality Organisation has reacted to the removal of a billboard bearing the photographs of President Bola Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti in Arochukwu Local Government Area of Abia State, dismissing suggestions of a political alliance among the three leaders and insisting that the former Abia governor neither erected nor commissioned the billboard.

The organisation, which called on the Nigeria Police Force and the Department of State Services (DSS) to closely monitor actions and utterances capable of heightening political tension in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections, maintained that individuals had the democratic right to support candidates across political party lines without their preferences being interpreted as evidence of a formal political alliance.

In a statement signed by Dimgba Okereke yesterday, the organisation disclosed that the billboard was the independent initiative of an Arochukwu indigene identified as Emeka, who chose to publicly identify with the three political leaders.

“For the avoidance of doubt, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu neither erected nor commissioned the billboard. It was the independent initiative of Engr. Emeka, a well-known son of Arochukwu, who chose to express his support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu and Governor Alex Otti.

“That is his personal choice and democratic right. His preference should not be misconstrued as evidence of a political alliance between the individuals or their respective political parties,” the organisation stated.

It maintained that Kalu’s political engagements over the decades had been anchored in grassroots mobilisation and direct interaction with the electorate rather than publicity materials.

“Senator Orji Uzor Kalu’s politics is anchored in the people, not billboards. For decades, he has maintained direct relationships with communities and ordinary citizens. His ongoing community-to-community engagements across Abia North are consistent with his longstanding approach to politics and representation.

“The OUK Movement and Reality Organisation have established grassroots structures built over several years through direct engagement with communities and voluntary participation by members and supporters.

“Senator Kalu cannot be held responsible for every independent expression of support by those who admire him. Neither can he be expected to stop individuals from expressing their political preferences within the confines of the law.”

While acknowledging the statutory responsibilities of advertising regulatory agencies, the organisation demanded fairness, transparency and political neutrality in the enforcement of advertising regulations, stressing that democracy thrived on freedom of choice, tolerance and respect for divergent political interests.

“Democracy is about the people and their freedom to make choices. A citizen’s decision to support candidates across political party lines does not necessarily amount to a formal political coalition.

“While we recognise the statutory responsibilities of advertising regulatory agencies, we expect such regulations to be applied fairly, transparently and without political discrimination.”

The organisation also urged its members and supporters to remain peaceful and resist any provocation while pursuing their legitimate political activities.

“We urge the Police and the DSS to pay careful attention to actions and utterances capable of creating unnecessary political tension in the state.

“We equally urge members of Reality Organisation to remain peaceful, disciplined and resolute in their lawful grassroots engagements without allowing themselves to be provoked by the actions of others.

“Ultimately, elections are determined by the electorate, not by billboards or their removal. The democratic right of the people to freely choose their representatives must remain paramount,” the statement concluded.
